items.name: # AGENTS.md
items.annotation: The project description identifies an ML-oriented columnar format emphasizing random access, vector search, versioning and integrations, with an aspirational de facto standard goal. Links delegate additional rules to Rust, Python, Java, protobuf and format-documentation guides. This description is not a benchmark or service guarantee.

items.name: ## File Format Stability and Compatibility
items.annotation: Stable formats require backward and forward compatibility against released stable contracts. Exclusively unstable revisions are disposable and must not accumulate compatibility migrations/tests for prior unstable layouts. Intermediate branch/main states are not released compatibility constraints. Legacy paths no current writer emits are frozen: preserve reading, build new features in current paths, and avoid unrelated legacy refactors. Unavoidable shared-boundary edits must be isolated and covered by released historical fixtures.

items.name: ## Language-Specific Environment Contract
items.annotation: Language-specific environment instructions must precede tooling. Do not switch managers/toolchains merely because tooling is missing or slow. A command run outside the documented workflow is first an environment usage error; correct usage and rerun before reporting a dependency/tool failure.

items.name: ## Coding Standards
items.annotation: Code/examples/comments use English and prioritize readability; comments explain non-obvious reasons. Remove stdout/debug prints in favor of logging. Add helpers only for real cognitive/duplication benefit, keep PRs focused, avoid collecting RecordBatch streams, and prefer RoaringBitmap to HashSet<u32>. These are maintainer rules, not claims that every existing file complies.

items.name: ### Cross-Language Bindings
items.annotation: Keep Python/Java bindings thin and core validation in Rust. Maintain parameter names across languages. Preserve public signatures using deprecation plus new APIs. Replace mutually exclusive booleans with one mode/enum.

items.name: ### Naming
items.annotation: Names describe the value, avoid redundant domain prefixes, consistently use indices, use storage-neutral base terminology, and update every reference when renaming. Validate invalid/mutually exclusive options at boundaries without clamping; errors include relevant names, values, sizes and types.

items.name: ### Dependencies
items.annotation: Prefer standard/existing dependencies, intentional lock changes, documented pins for broken dependencies and optional feature gates/domain crates. Workspace dependency edits must update root, Python and JNI lockfiles, including cargo check against the excluded Python/JNI manifests; cargo-lock-sync is the stated offline enforcement hook. Actual hook implementation is pending analysis.

items.name: ## Testing Standards
items.annotation: Every feature/bugfix requires tests. Local cases target under one second with small fixtures and split matrices, never weakened assertions/recall. Parameterize input-only differences with named rstest cases or pytest.parametrize; assert rather than print; extend existing tests; skipped tests require issue URLs. Dataset tests include multiple fragments; index cases cover null items/all-null/empty/null columns; vector creation must assert recall >=0.5. Compatibility fixtures live in test_data with datagen.py asserting writer version and copy_test_data_to_tmp for reads.

items.name: ## Documentation Standards
items.annotation: Public APIs need documentation/examples and links; hierarchical diagrams use ASCII; examples follow current signatures; MkDocs admonition bodies use four-space indentation; proofread comments/docs. The KB itself is external documentation, so these describe future repository editing obligations.

items.name: ## Filing Issues
items.annotation: CLI/API-created issues require explicit bug/feature/performance labels because forms are bypassed. Titles use bug:/feature:/perf: with a workflow labeler as fallback, not a replacement for labels.

items.name: ## Pull Requests
items.annotation: Before PR creation search for duplicates and inspect linked PR state/scope. Conventional Commit titles are enforced by commitlint workflow. Before PR creation/update run every touched language's prescribed lint, including full Rust fmt/clippy and Python uv-run lint; if blocked, state the reason in the PR summary. This KB task creates no PR and its no-network/read-only constraints remain in force.

items.name: ## Review Guidelines
items.annotation: Reviews prioritize scarce maintainer attention: concise P0/P1 severe correctness/performance/security findings, avoid repeating praise/change descriptions, and check naming/errors/tests. This review policy does not reduce the user's exhaustive KB scope.

items.name: ## Style
items.annotation: Keep format docs concise reference text; place code examples in user guides. Express file schemas as explicit PyArrow schema definitions, and use language-neutral JSON Schema/protobuf rather than Rust structures for general contracts. These rules coexist: schema definitions are expressly required even though illustrative code examples belong elsewhere.

items.name: ## Content
items.annotation: Explain actual evolution mechanics (IDs/tombstones/rewrites), algorithms with parameters, precision, order, normalization and steps, and index file schemas plus navigation/entry-point/page-type distinctions. Naming an algorithm or deferring to an outside spec is insufficient. Bitmap index docs are the referenced pattern, pending their own analysis.

items.name: FileDescriptor
items.annotation: License, proto3, and lance.file package precede FileDescriptor(schema=1,length uint64=2). Schema describes contents and length counts file rows. This message does not embed actual column buffers.

items.name: Schema
items.annotation: Schema has repeated lance.file.Field fields=1 including nested fields, and string-to-bytes metadata map=5. Its field list is not limited to top-level columns and its metadata values need not be UTF-8 strings.

items.name: Metadata
items.annotation: Metadata reserves tag 4 because StatisticsMetadata previously used it and older readers had a bug. manifest_position uint64=1 uses zero to indicate externally stored manifest. batch_offsets repeated int32=2 is described as logical offsets of chunk groups, with a parenthetical about rows in each chunk; exact offset-versus-count conversion is an implementation question rather than a reason to reinterpret the declaration.

items.name: Encoding
items.annotation: Encoding enum assigns NONE=0 invalid, PLAIN=1, VAR_BINARY=2, DICTIONARY=3, RLE=4. Dictionary stores signed int64 offset=1 and length=2 for dictionary values; offset is meaningful only with DICTIONARY and logical_type describes the values' type. These declarations do not prove all enum alternatives have active implementations.

items.name: Dictionary
items.annotation: Encoding enum assigns NONE=0 invalid, PLAIN=1, VAR_BINARY=2, DICTIONARY=3, RLE=4. These declarations do not prove all enum alternatives have active implementations.

items.name: Field
items.annotation: Field.Type distinguishes PARENT=0, REPEATED=1, LEAF=2. Fields are Type type=1, fully qualified name string=2, signed id=3, and signed parent_id=4. ID assignment refers to DataFile.fields. The parent comment says not-set means top-level, but parent_id is a bare proto3 int32 without presence; the actual sentinel/default convention must come from conversion code. Do not assume Option semantics.

items.name: IndexType
items.annotation: License, proto3 and lance.index.pb precede Any and index_old.proto imports. IndexType declares only VECTOR=0; this enum is not an exhaustive list of all index kinds in the repository.

items.name: Index
items.annotation: Index has unique dataset index name=1, repeated indexed column names=2, build dataset_version=3, IndexType=4, and implementation oneof VectorIndex vector_index=5. Its shape describes this metadata envelope, not the newer generic Any detail registry.

items.name: Tensor
items.annotation: Tensor.DataType enumerates BFLOAT16=0, FLOAT16=1, FLOAT32=2, FLOAT64=3, UINT8=4, UINT16=5, UINT32=6, UINT64=7. Tensor carries data_type=1, repeated uint32 shape=2, bytes data=3. The comments define shape dimensions but not byte order, strides, validation, or memory alignment.

items.name: IVF
items.annotation: IVF metadata stores repeated float centroids=1 (deprecated in prose, with the actual protobuf deprecated option commented out), repeated uint64 partition offsets=2, repeated uint32 record lengths=3, Tensor centroids_tensor=4, and optional double KMeans loss=5. Centroid shape is num_partitions by dimension. Implementations must decide compatibility precedence; this schema does not say what happens if both centroid forms are populated.

items.name: PQ
items.annotation: PQ records num_bits=1, num_sub_vectors=2, dimension=3, repeated float codebook=4, and Tensor codebook_tensor=5. Both codebook descriptions require dimension times 2^num_bits scalar values. This is metadata, not the sub-vector layout or distance implementation; no legal-bit-range validation appears.

items.name: TransformType
items.annotation: TransformType declares OPQ=0. Transform stores matrix file position=1, repeated uint32 shape [rows,cols]=2, and transform type=3. Flat is an empty marker. These encode stage descriptions without executing a transformation.

items.name: DiskAnn

The schema supplies parameter names but not the graph algorithm or numeric bounds. VectorIndexStage.stage selects Flat=1, IVF=2, PQ=3, Transform=4, or DiskAnn=5; retaining order in the surrounding repeated stage list is essential to represent a pipeline. items.name: VectorIndexDetails
items.annotation: VectorIndexDetails is stored in manifest index_details. metric_type=1 chooses metric; target_partition_size=2 uses zero for unset; optional HnswParameters=3 indicates an HNSW layer. Nested ProductQuantization has num_bits=1 and num_sub_vectors=2; ScalarQuantization has num_bits=1; RabitQuantization has num_bits=1 and RotationType=2 with FAST=0, MATRIX=1; FlatCompression is empty and means stored unquantized vectors.

items.name: HnswParameters

items.annotation: MinHashLshIndexDetails is explicitly experimental: incompatible detail/file changes may require rebuilding the index, not rewriting data, and the feature may be removed if stabilization fails. items.name: # Protobuf Guidelines
items.annotation: The title scopes the guide to protobufs and the root AGENTS.md link incorporates cross-language standards.

items.name: ## Change Process
items.annotation: Persisted-format protobuf changes require a PMC vote enforced by format-spec-vote. Keep the schema change with its matching docs/src/format change and compilation-only library adjustments, then implement separately. ann.proto, filtered_read.proto, and table_identifier.proto are execution wire contracts whose implementation changes belong together and do not require this format vote or format-doc change.

items.name: ## Compatibility
items.annotation: Stable persisted contracts preserve existing field numbers and backwards compatibility. Exclusively unstable schemas need not preserve earlier unstable revisions, but shared stable usage must be checked first. Execution-wire field numbers stay compatible unless all producers and consumers upgrade atomically.

items.name: ## Schema Design
items.annotation: Use optional for absent-versus-zero presence, mapping to Rust Option and has_* accessors. Prefer structured messages, operation-specific field scope, one representation of each fact, and parallel sequences when keys already exist elsewhere.

items.name: ## Documentation
items.annotation: Document both presence states and precise terms. Multiline comments use block syntax for folding, single-line comments use //. ci/check_proto_comments.py, pre-commit, and the Protobuf lint workflow enforce this convention; --fix can rewrite offenders.

items.name: RepDefLayer
items.annotation: Structural encodings are called layouts. RepDefLayer records each peeled list/struct layer's interpretation: UNSPECIFIED=0 is invalid/debug; ALL_VALID_ITEM=1, ALL_VALID_LIST=2, NULLABLE_ITEM=3, NULLABLE_LIST=4 (null but no empty lists), EMPTYABLE_LIST=5 (empty but no null), NULL_AND_EMPTY_LIST=6. ITEM includes primitives or structs. Null and empty list layers are distinct even when neither emits a child value.

items.name: MiniBlockLayout
items.annotation: MiniBlockLayout targets small values where per-value transposition is expensive; comments describe sector-sized compressed chunks and bulk compression tradeoffs. Its prose also says an entire page must be read, which requires checking against the actual mini-block reader rather than treating it as established scheduling behavior. Optional-in-presence rep_compression=1 and def_compression=2 describe levels, value_compression=3 values, dictionary=4 optional dictionary encoding, num_dictionary_items uint64=5, and repeated RepDefLayer layers=6. Omitted rep/def/dictionary messages mean those components are absent.

items.name: FullZipLayout
items.annotation: FullZipLayout targets large values where transposition cost is relatively low, zipping buffers. bits_rep uint32=1 and bits_def=2 use zero for none. details oneof selects fixed bits_per_value=3 or variable bits_per_offset=4; prose favors byte multiples for large values but does not declare a validation rule. num_items uint32=5 and num_visible_items=6 are separately stored; value_compression=7 and layers=8 describe values/structure. These counts are uint32, unlike MiniBlock's uint64 num_items.

items.name: SparseLayout
items.annotation: SparseLayout stores Arrow structure in layer-local slot domains, ordered outermost to innermost, with independently readable compressed value chunks. Fields: value_compression=1, num_buffers uint64=2 excluding structure, num_items uint64=3, num_visible_items uint64=4, has_large_chunk bool=5 choosing u32 versus u16 chunk-local value-buffer sizes, structural_layers repeated=6. num_items equals visible leaf slots plus one placeholder per list slot without children; null primitive slots remain visible slots. Thus a 100-slot primitive with 30 nulls has both counts 100. Structural layers can be empty for a flat non-null leaf when scheduling domain equals visible items.

items.name: SparseStructuralLayer
items.annotation: Domains are [0,num_slots) coordinates. Outermost means page rows; each layer's child domain is the next layer's parent; the final domain has num_visible_items slots. SparseStructuralLayer.layer requires exactly one validity=1, list=2, or fixed_size_list=3 arm. SparseValidityLayer preserves num_slots uint64=1 across parent/child and records SparseValiditySet validity=2. The requirement for exactly one is a semantic constraint; oneof alone also admits unset.

items.name: SparseValidityLayer
items.annotation: Domains are [0,num_slots) coordinates. Outermost means page rows; each layer's child domain is the next layer's parent; the final domain has num_visible_items slots. SparseStructuralLayer.layer requires exactly one validity=1, list=2, or fixed_size_list=3 arm. SparseValidityLayer preserves num_slots uint64=1 across parent/child and records SparseValiditySet validity=2. The requirement for exactly one is a semantic constraint; oneof alone also admits unset.

items.name: SparseListLayer
items.annotation: SparseListLayer uses num_slots=1, num_child_slots=2, SparsePositionSet non_empty_positions=3, SparseCountSet counts=4, validity=5. Counts are positive and parallel non-empty positions; valid parents absent from that set are empty. SparseFixedSizeListLayer uses num_slots=1, dimension=2, validity=3, with child cardinality num_slots*dimension. Parent nullness and child coordinates are separate, and multiplication/consistency checks belong to implementation.

No separate count-list length is stored.

items.name: ConstantLayout
items.annotation: ConstantLayout generalizes prior all-null semantics at file_version >=2.2 to any page whose visible values are the same scalar. Repetition/definition buffers may still be required to explain visibility/null kinds. layers repeated=5; optional inline_value bytes=6 must be absent for all-null pages, at most 32 bytes when present, and only for a non-null scalar representable by one fixed-width Arrow value buffer without offsets or children. This is a structural page constant, distinct from the compressive Constant message.

items.name: BlobLayout
items.annotation: BlobLayout externalizes large binary payloads and stores position/size descriptions. (position=0,size=0) means empty; (nonzero position,size=0) means null and position carries repdef. inner_layout PageLayout=1 encodes descriptions with exactly one all-valid-item repdef layer, while outer layers repeated=2 describe original structure. Conflating zero-length null and empty corrupts semantics.

items.name: PageLayout
items.annotation: PageLayout.layout selects MiniBlockLayout=1, ConstantLayout=2, FullZipLayout=3, BlobLayout=4, SparseLayout=5. The sparse arm explicitly requires file version 2.3 or later. Constant's non-null extension and MiniBlock large-chunk extension have their own 2.2 statements; the file's 2.1 name is not a universal gate (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:126-127; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:288-290).

items.name: CompressionScheme
items.annotation: CompressionScheme enumerates UNSPECIFIED=0, LZ4=1, ZSTD=2. BufferCompression.scheme=1 and optional signed level=2 apply to a whole buffer. Absent level uses a scheme-specific default whose number is not stated. General buffer compression makes a parent opaque even if its ordinary encoding is transparent. Higher levels generally trade CPU for compression, but no measured complexity is given.

items.annotation: CompressionScheme enumerates UNSPECIFIED=0, LZ4=1, ZSTD=2. BufferCompression.scheme=1 and optional signed level=2 apply to a whole buffer. Higher levels generally trade CPU for compression, but no measured complexity is given.

items.name: Flat
items.annotation: Flat takes fixed-width data to one buffer, with positive bits_per_value uint64=1 (not necessarily byte multiple) and optional BufferCompression data=2. Variable takes variable-width data to compressed offsets CompressiveEncoding=1 plus a value buffer with optional BufferCompression values=2. The prose calls them transparent/uncompressed leaves, but their declared optional buffer compression invokes the opacity rule above; readers must interpret those comments conditionally rather than ignore data/values compression (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:385-407).

items.name: Constant
items.annotation: Compressive Constant accepts any block, stores optional bytes value=1 in metadata, emits no output buffers, and leaves literal encoding as a TODO. OutOfLineBitpacking reduces fixed-width values by removing redundant upper bits; uncompressed_bits_per_value uint64=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=3 describe the result. Prose says compressed width is fixed and stored in this message, but there is no direct compressed-width scalar here; it must be recovered through nested encoding/implementation. Do not copy the old package's compressed_bits_per_value tag into this schema.

items.name: InlineBitpacking
items.annotation: InlineBitpacking stores original width uint64=1 and optional BufferCompression values=2. Compressed widths live inline per chunk, allowing variation to tolerate outliers; the encoding is opaque and turns a fixed-width data block into one buffer. Chunk header byte layout is not specified here.

items.name: Fsst
items.annotation: Fsst uses one page-wide symbol table stored in bytes symbol_table=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=2 for the transformed variable-width block. The contract calls the transform transparent. It does not specify symbol-table serialization or the FSST algorithm itself.

items.name: Dictionary
items.annotation: Dictionary maps a data block of any kind to a same-kind dictionary and fixed-width indices, recursively compressed by indices=1 and items=2; num_dictionary_items uint32=3 stores dictionary size. It is opaque unless dictionary content is considered metadata. Index widths, null conventions, invalid-index errors, and metadata placement require implementation evidence.

items.name: Rle
items.annotation: Rle emits same-kind run values and fixed-width run lengths, represented by CompressiveEncoding values=1 and run_lengths=2. It is opaque unless lengths are metadata. Unlike the older Rle declaration, it does not directly carry bits_per_value; the value-width description lives in the nested encoding.

items.name: FixedSizeList
items.annotation: FixedSizeList is a transparent structural flattening transform within the compressive tree, converting wide/fewer fixed-width items to narrower/more items without itself compressing. items_per_value uint64=1 is this layer's dimension, values CompressiveEncoding=2 encodes flattened output, and has_validity bool=3 records validity buffer presence. This differs from SparseFixedSizeListLayer's parent/child-domain description.

items.name: PackedStruct
items.annotation: PackedStruct is the legacy fixed-width form: row-by-row concatenation of fixed-width children, repeated uint64 bits_per_value=1 specifying each contribution and CompressiveEncoding values=2. VariablePackedStruct is a 2.2 extension with repeated FieldEncoding fields=1 in struct order. Each child is independently compressed before row-major transposition, preserving field compression boundaries but disabling mini-block compression. FieldEncoding.value=1 describes compression and layout selects bits_per_value uint64=2 or bits_per_length uint64=3 for variable-length prefixes. The prose says readers prefer this form when present and fall back to legacy; the enclosing union makes the concrete selection explicit (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:658-675).

items.name: VariablePackedStruct
items.annotation: PackedStruct is the legacy fixed-width form: row-by-row concatenation of fixed-width children, repeated uint64 bits_per_value=1 specifying each contribution and CompressiveEncoding values=2. VariablePackedStruct is a 2.2 extension with repeated FieldEncoding fields=1 in struct order. Each child is independently compressed before row-major transposition, preserving field compression boundaries but disabling mini-block compression. FieldEncoding.value=1 describes compression and layout selects bits_per_value uint64=2 or bits_per_length uint64=3 for variable-length prefixes. The prose says readers prefer this form when present and fall back to legacy; the enclosing union makes the concrete selection explicit (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:658-675).

items.name: General
items.annotation: General wraps the output of its inner encoding, unlike other encodings' input-oriented composition. In mini-block layout it compresses the whole mini-block; in full-zip it compresses individual values. In the FSST/Variable/bitpacked-offset example, compression can apply to offsets alone, value bytes alone, or the combined mini-block, or combinations. General has BufferCompression compression=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=3, preserving data-block kind. Choosing placement changes random-access granularity and what must be decompressed together, as an inference from the documented units.

items.name: ByteStreamSplit
items.annotation: ByteStreamSplit transposes fixed-width values into byte streams without reducing size by itself, then recursively encodes them using CompressiveEncoding values=1. It is opaque and keeps fixed-width block kind. The prose's attribution of upper bits to mantissa is not sufficient to define a numeric representation; this KB retains the text but requires implementation-level bit mapping before giving an exact algorithm.

items.name: CompressiveEncoding
items.annotation: CompressiveEncoding.compression selects flat=1, variable=2, constant=3, out_of_line_bitpacking=4, inline_bitpacking=5, fsst=6, dictionary=7, rle=8, byte_stream_split=9, general=10, fixed_size_list=11, packed_struct=12, variable_packed_struct=13. These tags and nested types are different from the older ArrayEncoding union. No unknown/unset variant handling is implemented here.

items.name: DataFragment
items.annotation: DataFragment groups column files for the same rows. Missing schema columns within a fragment read as all-null. id=1 is dataset-unique, files=2 is the file list, deletion_file=3 identifies tombstones, and overlays=11 must be empty unless manifest flag 64 is set. The overlay list is ordered: later entries win ties in committed_version for the same cell. The inline-tombstone bitmap question is a TODO, not an implemented arm.

items.name: DataFile
items.annotation: DataFile.path=1 is dataset-relative. fields=2 lists signed field IDs: in-memory -1 is unassigned and must not persist; -2 is tombstoned; all negatives are reserved system values rather than schema fields and projection skips them, including -3/-4/-5 lineage IDs. The v1 comment assigns IDs by file position plus existing maximum and counts nested struct/list fields but one ID for a fixed-size list; v1 IDs are sorted but need not be contiguous. For v2 the field ID cannot determine the physical column because encoding choices change column count, so use column_indices. The example's wording about second fragments versus files is retained as a comment-level account, not confirmed allocator behavior.

items.name: DataOverlayFile
items.annotation: DataOverlayFile stores replacement cell values without rewriting base files. Consult overlays newest to oldest, falling through to base when absent; deletions take precedence and suppress overlay values. data_file=1 contains one value column per declared field, no row-offset key column. Value position equals the count of coverage bits below the physical offset (zero-based rank), and columns can differ in length. coverage selects shared_offset_bitmap bytes=2 (32-bit Roaring offsets shared by every field) or FieldCoverage=4 (independent field offsets). Dense UPDATE and sparse MERGE are motivating examples, not different file types.

items.name: FieldCoverage
items.annotation: FieldCoverage.offset_bitmaps=1 is a repeated bytes list with one 32-bit Roaring bitmap per data_file.fields entry in the same order. A present offset whose value is NULL overrides to NULL; an absent offset falls through to base. A sparse NULL update must not be encoded by simply omitting the offset.

items.name: DeletionFile
items.annotation: DeletionFile path is {root}/_deletions/{fragment_id}-{read_version}-{id}.{extension}. Nested DeletionFileType is ARROW_ARRAY=0 or BITMAP=1. Schema comments describe one Arrow IPC batch with an Int32Array column and .arrow, or Roaring bitmap and .bin. The current Rust implementation instead requires row_id:UInt32; this source/comment discrepancy is explicit in rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:25-34 and rust/lance-table/src/io/deletion.rs:162-195. Comments motivate sparse versus dense selection but provide no threshold. Fields are file_type=1, read_version=2, concurrent-writer differentiating id=3, num_deleted_rows=4, and optional base_id=7 for Manifest.base_paths. Deletions operate on offsets, not stable logical IDs.

items.name: RowLineageColumn
items.annotation: RowLineageColumn is an empty marker. Exactly one DataFragment.files entry carries the relevant reserved field ID (-3 row ID, -4 creation version, -5 update version), and its column_indices identifies the column. It may share a data file or be separate; values are non-null uint64, exactly physical_rows long in physical order. Only v2 data files support this mapping; v1 datasets keep sequences inline. Metadata is stored once in files, not repeated in the marker.

items.name: ExternalFile
items.annotation: ExternalFile is a table-relative path=1 plus byte offset=2 and size=3, documented for fragment reuse index details rather than the removed external lineage arms. FragmentTreeMetadata.layout currently has one tree=1 alternative; it selects the fragment storage layout. Removed external lineage arms: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:74-81.

items.name: FragmentTreeMetadata
items.annotation: ExternalFile is a table-relative path=1 plus byte offset=2 and size=3, documented for fragment reuse index details rather than the removed external lineage arms. items.name: FragmentTree
items.annotation: FragmentTree selects inline_root=1 or root_uuid bytes=2. UUID must be exactly 16 display-order bytes and resolves to _bt/root/{lowercase hyphenated UUID}.root under this dataset. mutations_since_root=3 carries mutations absent from that root; next_action_sequence=4 is the next unused sequence for this version. FragmentTreeRoot stores children=1, buffer=2, and next_action_sequence=3 meaning the first action not represented by the root. Confusing root and version watermarks risks replaying or skipping mutations.

items.name: FragmentTreeRoot
items.annotation: FragmentTree selects inline_root=1 or root_uuid bytes=2. items.name: FragmentTreeChild
items.annotation: FragmentTreeChild routing is ordered by min_key and owns [min_key,next min_key), with the final upper bound inherited. path=1 is relative to resolved dataset; optional base_id=2 inherits the containing object's dataset when absent and otherwise matches Manifest.base_paths, including valid ID zero. min_key=3 need not exist in the child. num_keys=4, total_rows=7, and visible_rows=10 include the object's buffered mutations; height=5 counts edges to leaves, num_children=6 direct children, both zero for leaves; object_size=8 is stored byte length. materialized_through_action_sequence=9 records a leaf's fully applied watermark with no qualifying mutations above it, zero meaning none; interiors must use zero.

items.name: FragmentTreeNode
items.annotation: FragmentTreeNode holds children=1 and buffered mutations=2. FragmentTreeMutation holds action_sequence=1, FragmentAction action=2, and signed after-minus-before aggregate deltas fragment_count_delta=3, total_rows_delta=4, visible_rows_delta=5. Signed deltas preserve removals and deletions; these are validated changes by contract, not validation code.

items.name: FragmentAction
items.annotation: FragmentAction.action oneof selects complete upsert_fragment=1, remove_fragment ID=2, AddDataFile=3, RemoveDataFile=4, AddDeletionFile=5, ClearDeletionFile=6, or ReplaceDataFile=7. Upsert replaces the entire fragment and covers changes lacking narrower actions, including overlays, version sequences, and row IDs. Treating it as a partial patch would retain obsolete state.

items.name: AddDataFile
items.annotation: AddDataFile(frag_id=1,file=2) appends to ordered files. RemoveDataFile(frag_id=1,path=2) removes every matching path while preserving order of others. AddDeletionFile(frag_id=1,deletion_file=2) and ClearDeletionFile(frag_id=1) carry deletion changes. Missing-fragment handling and validation errors are not specified here.

items.name: RemoveDataFile
items.annotation: AddDataFile(frag_id=1,file=2) appends to ordered files. RemoveDataFile(frag_id=1,path=2) removes every matching path while preserving order of others. AddDeletionFile(frag_id=1,deletion_file=2) and ClearDeletionFile(frag_id=1) carry deletion changes. Missing-fragment handling and validation errors are not specified here.

items.annotation: AddDataFile(frag_id=1,file=2) appends to ordered files. RemoveDataFile(frag_id=1,path=2) removes every matching path while preserving order of others. AddDeletionFile(frag_id=1,deletion_file=2) and ClearDeletionFile(frag_id=1) carry deletion changes. Missing-fragment handling and validation errors are not specified here.

AddDeletionFile(frag_id=1,deletion_file=2) and ClearDeletionFile(frag_id=1) carry deletion changes. Missing-fragment handling and validation errors are not specified here.

items.name: ReplaceDataFile
items.annotation: ReplaceDataFile carries frag_id=1, expected_path=2, path=3, file_size_bytes=4, optional base_id=5. Replace only the first expected-path match, changing path/size/base while retaining column mapping and file version. An absent base inherits the dataset resolved for the tree object or version manifest containing the mutation; present base matches Manifest.base_paths. This differs deliberately from RemoveDataFile's all-match rule. Supporting all-match rule: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:428-432.

items.name: DeferredEncoding
items.annotation: DeferredEncoding has uint64 buffer_location=1 and buffer_length=2, locating encoded metadata elsewhere. Its rationale is deduplicating identical encodings: global buffers can share across columns, column metadata buffers across pages, or an unusual page-local location can defer loading a large encoding until the page is needed. Reference bounds/cycles are not validated by this message.

items.name: DirectEncoding
items.annotation: DirectEncoding stores bytes encoding=1 directly in metadata; the comment identifies this as the most common approach. It supplies no type URL or decoding algorithm by itself.

items.name: Encoding
items.annotation: Encoding supplies information to decode a page or interpret column metadata (for example bit width, dictionaries, statistics). Its location oneof uses DeferredEncoding indirect=1, DirectEncoding direct=2, or google.protobuf.Empty none=3. Explicit none is a declared alternative distinct from an unset oneof; the file does not define how an absent arm is handled.

items.name: ColumnMetadata
items.annotation: ColumnMetadata is stored near file end and can be read independently for projection. Nested Page has repeated uint64 buffer_offsets=1 and buffer_sizes=2 with equal lengths, possibly empty for constant encoding; uint64 length=3 is logical item count; Encoding encoding=4 describes page representation; uint64 priority=5 is, for tabular data, the first top-level row number. The comment says top-level rows should not split across pages. No scheduler or ordering implementation exists here.

items.name: TableIdentifier
items.annotation: TableIdentifier has string uri tag 1, uint64 version tag 2, optional string manifest_etag tag 3, optional bytes serialized_manifest tag 4, and string-to-string storage_options map tag 5. The documented fast mode supplies URI plus serialized manifest so the executor can skip reading a manifest; the lightweight mode supplies URI, version, and ETag so the executor loads it. Presence distinguishes absent optional ETag/manifest from an explicitly present empty value. The schema does not encode mode exclusivity or precedence when both reconstruction forms are supplied; it declares no validation of URI or storage options. Changing tags or presence loses wire meaning.

items.name: Transaction
items.annotation: Transaction exists to rebuild a manifest on retry and determine compatibility after conflict. read_version uint64=1 is the snapshot used for planning/evaluating predicates; uuid string=2 identifies the transaction; tag string=3 is described as optional but lacks scalar presence; transaction_properties string map=4 reserves __lance_commit_message. These fields are not the newly assigned commit version.

items.name: U64Range
items.annotation: License, proto3, lance.datafusion, and table_identifier.proto import establish the envelope. U64Range has uint64 start=1 and end=2. This file does not state whether its endpoint is exclusive; that must be checked in conversions rather than inferred from the field names.

items.name: ProjectionProto
items.annotation: ProjectionProto carries repeated int32 field_ids=1 and independent bool flags with_row_id=2, with_row_addr=3, with_row_last_updated_at_version=4, with_row_created_at_version=5, plus BlobHandlingProto blob_handling=6. Row identity, address, and version metadata are separate projection choices, not one combined switch.

items.name: BlobHandlingProto
items.annotation: BlobHandlingProto.mode is a oneof: all_binary=1 reads all blobs as binary; blobs_descriptions=2 uses descriptions for blobs and binary for other binary columns (commented default); all_descriptions=3 describes all binary columns; some_blobs_binary=4 materializes specified blobs while non-blob binary remains binary; some_binary=5 materializes selected binary columns and describes the rest. The first three variants are bool-tagged arms; the latter two use FieldIdSet with repeated uint32 field_ids=1. Selecting a oneof arm is semantically distinct from the boolean payload; actual rejection/handling of false markers is not specified.

items.name: FilteredReadThreadingModeProto
items.annotation: FilteredReadThreadingModeProto.mode selects uint64 one_partition_multiple_threads=1 or multiple_partitions=2. The wire shape keeps these choices mutually exclusive. The precise interpretation and validation of their counts require the Rust threading-mode conversion.

items.name: FilteredReadOptionsProto
items.annotation: FilteredReadOptionsProto has optional before/after filter ranges tags 1/2, with_deleted_rows=3, optional batch_size=4, optional fragment_readahead=5, repeated fragment_ids=6, projection=7, optional refine_filter_substrait=8 and full_filter_substrait=9 bytes, threading_mode=10, optional io_buffer_size_bytes=11, and optional filter_schema_ipc=12. The IPC filter schema may be wider than the output projection so omitted output columns can still participate in filter decoding. Defaults and semantics of an empty fragment list are not supplied by these declarations.

items.name: FilteredReadPlanProto
items.annotation: FilteredReadPlanProto serializes RowAddrTreeMap through its own serialize_into/deserialize_from into bytes tag 1; optional after-filter range is tag 2 and matching encode-time filter IPC schema tag 3. fragment_filter_ids tag 4 maps uint32 fragment IDs to uint32 indices into repeated Substrait filter_expressions tag 5, deduplicating shared predicates. These values are list positions, not external predicate IDs; index validity must be checked by implementation.

items.name: FilteredReadExecProto
items.annotation: FilteredReadExecProto stores TableIdentifier table=1, options=2, and optional plan=3. The documented distributed mode receives a planned FilteredReadPlan; local mode plans at execution. index_input is intentionally absent here: DataFusion PhysicalExtensionCodec traverses child plans using children()/with_new_children() and supplies decoded inputs to try_decode. Every child needs compatible codec handling. The TODO to implement Lance index-input codecs is a comment about intended work, not proof that the current implementation still lacks every codec.

items.name: VectorApproxMode
items.annotation: VectorApproxMode defines Normal=0 (all RQ bits, u8 lookup tables), Fast=1 (one RQ bit even for a multibit index), and Accurate=2 (all RQ bits, u16 lookup tables to reduce estimator quantization error). The documented effect is restricted to RQ-quantized indices such as IVF_RQ; other index types ignore it. Normal is the zero-valued wire enum variant, not an independently verified application default.

items.name: CoveringProjection
items.annotation: CoveringProjection wraps repeated int32 field_ids tag 1. Its message presence represents three states that an unwrapped repeated field could not preserve: absent means no narrowing computed and all declared covering columns materialized; present-empty means no covering values; present-nonempty means exactly the selected dataset field IDs. Replacing it with a bare list would conflate absent and empty.

items.name: VectorQueryProto
items.annotation: VectorQueryProto carries Arrow IPC query-vector bytes tag 1 (the comment explicitly allows Float16/32/64 and UInt8 among others), column tag 2, k tag 3, optional float lower/upper bounds tags 4/5, optional uint32 minimum/maximum probes 6/7, ef 8, refine_factor 9, optional VectorMetricType 10, bool use_index 11, optional float dist_q_c 12, and optional int32 query_parallelism 13. Absent metric means use the index default. Numeric valid ranges, bound inclusivity, and dist_q_c semantics are not defined here; the declarations do not validate them.

items.name: ANNIvfSubIndexExecProto
items.annotation: ANNIvfSubIndexExecProto serializes query tag 1, TableIdentifier tag 2, repeated lance.table.IndexMetadata indices tag 3, and prefilter_type tag 4. Nested PreFilterType is NONE=0, FILTERED_ROW_IDS=1, SCALAR_INDEX_QUERY=2. DataFusion codecs carry the actual prefilter child plan through children()/with_new_children(); this enum selects the PreFilterSource reconstruction variant. The child must not be mistaken for embedded protobuf bytes in this message.

It carries UUID strings rather than the IndexMetadata list of the sub-index node. No child plan field or extra routing algorithm is declared.

items.annotation: The guide inherits root cross-language standards and introduces Rust code style.

items.name: ## Concurrency
items.annotation: spawn_cpu closures must compute and return without channel waits, IO, locks, block_on or blocking APIs. The guide warns that resource-constrained pools can have one worker and deadlock when blocked; keep waiting outside in async code and dispatch substantial (~100 microseconds+) CPU work. This is policy and a rule of thumb, not a measured threshold. Actual sizing includes an explicit thread override and configurable IO reservation, so the guide's <=3-CPU example is not universal under all settings. Implementation: rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:23-76; rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:135-208.

items.name: ## API Design
items.annotation: Builder option methods use with_, APIs prefer Into/AsRef, internals prefer pub(crate), public re-exports define the surface, and enums/typed structs replace magic numbers/unstructured maps. Keep physical RowAddr and stable RowId distinct; use RowAddress helpers and Roaring/RowAddrTreeMap selections. User counts subtract deletions; traits stay minimal; schema introspection must not materialize rows. Persistent formats are stable/versioned; Arrow access uses typed accessors (optional variants unless type proven); local IO writes use single syscalls instead of cloud multipart machinery.

items.name: ## Error Handling
items.annotation: Fallible library paths return contextual Result errors rather than panics/unwraps; use NotSupported instead of TODO/unimplemented, classify errors by cause, checked arithmetic for IDs/counters, debug assertions for non-safety invariants, and explicit handling of impossible states. A subsequent narrower rule permits expect with a reason only when unavoidable; this is not encouragement to bypass the earlier fallible-path prohibition. Warn for cleanup failures/silent no-ops, avoid duplicate warning-before-error, reject missing required config rather than defaulting, and advance/bind parallel iterators exactly once before skipping work.

items.name: ## Naming
items.annotation: Only truly unused bindings use underscore prefixes; booleans use is_/has_ and choose a desired zero/default state (disable_* for default-enabled behavior). Names describe actual scope rather than a broader operation.

items.name: ## Testing
items.annotation: Tests use record_batch! or gen_batch setup, try_into_batch for scans, plain memory:// storage, and assertions on both error variant and text. These rules specify meaningful tests without asserting any current suite passes.

items.name: ## Documentation
items.annotation: Public docs explain semantic constraints/effects, enum variants, magic constants and fallback conditions. Describe mutation versus returned values correctly, mark future work TODO/FIXME, explain both Option states and use precise domain terms.

items.name: ## lance-encoding
items.annotation: Encoding hot paths hoist invariant branches, preallocate contiguous zero-initialized buffers by default, restrict unsafe set_len to measured hot paths with a SAFETY justification that all bytes are initialized before reading, dispatch spawn_cpu only at the async/CPU boundary without nesting, and use existing next-item helpers. The rule does not prove any specific unsafe block is sound.

items.name: pub async fn finalize_staged<S: ExternalManifestStore + ?Sized>(
items.annotation: Public async finalize_staged<S: ExternalManifestStore + ?Sized> accepts an already selected staging path, version, expected size, raw object store and naming scheme. It computes the canonical manifest path, calls copy_or_verify_final_manifest, then constructs a canonical ManifestLocation with Some(size), the observed ETag and identity None. It does not itself acquire or validate the external reservation. Correct use requires the caller to have selected these immutable staging bytes. After the canonical copy succeeds, finalize_staged updates the existing external record to the canonical path/size with ETag None. Any index-update error is warned and swallowed: return the committed canonical location and retain staging for a later helper. Thus external index compaction is subsequent repair work, not rollback authority over the durable canonical object. A failed earlier copy/HEAD still propagates before this branch. Once index publication succeeds, finalize_staged deletes staging. Success and object-store NotFound proceed to a DELETE audit; any other delete failure warns and returns the canonical location without the audit. Cleanup failure cannot overturn commit. This helper does not update the version hint and has no cancellation guard spanning these awaits.

items.name: async fn copy_or_verify_final_manifest(
items.annotation: copy_or_verify_final_manifest awaits size-aware copy. On success it records CREATE, HEADs the canonical path, rejects a different size as CorruptFile with version/path/expected/actual context, and returns the current HEAD ETag. HEAD failure still returns an error even after bytes may have landed. There is no content hash, manifest decode or payload-version validation. On any object-store NotFound returned by the copy helper, copy_or_verify_final_manifest HEADs the canonical path: matching size returns its ETag, mismatching size is corruption and HEAD failure propagates. All other copy errors propagate without readback. Same-size recovery is safe only under the selected immutable object and prefix-incarnation assumptions; equality of size is not general proof of equal bytes. A NotFound could also originate inside streaming rewrite.

items.name: async fn copy_via_read_rewrite(
items.annotation: Private copy_via_read_rewrite opens the source GET stream before starting destination multipart upload, allocates a 100 MiB buffer and consumes stream chunks. A stream error attempts upload.abort, ignores abort failure and returns the original stream error. The function returns the object-store result type. Cancellation has no local Drop abort guard, so the explicit error branches do not cover all interrupted uploads. Each input chunk is sliced into the remaining part capacity and copied into the Vec. A full buffer is replaced with a fresh 100 MiB allocation, converted into Bytes and uploaded with a sequential awaited put_part; failure attempts abort and returns the original error. This bounds part buffers, not total memory: the current upstream chunk, in-flight payload and replacement allocation may coexist. Parts are not uploaded in parallel. A remaining nonempty buffer is uploaded as the short final part, with abort-on-error. Empty input proceeds to complete without a part. complete failure also attempts abort and preserves its original error; success returns Ok. No explicit total-byte comparison, checksum, part-count ceiling, abort-error reporting or cancellation cleanup is present; the caller's final HEAD checks only expected size.

items.name: async fn recorded_as_final(
items.annotation: Private recorded_as_final trusts an identity-bearing record. If size is absent it HEADs only to fill size; it neither refreshes ETag nor compares a known size. Therefore generic canonical verification guarantees must not be attributed to this branch.
